title: Reading the other sections' parts while sitting on the stand
summary: He explains his habit of reading every part in the book so he would know when someone played a wrong note.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Fats -- yeah, Fats Waller came in to Smalls and saw me, happened to be in there in a little party, and saw me playing, and -- uh, I like this story too. I like this right here.

When Fats came in, I wasn't aware of it, because I didn't know him, I hadn't ever met Fats. I'm sitting on the stand, all the fellows -- most of the fellows had gotten up and gone here, gone there, gone over to the john, parties, wherever, whatnot. I sat on the stage by myself, and I dunno, I was just like -- if I'm playing a part, okay. I'm in this band, I'm playing first. This particular tune, well I knew what could happen, see, because
I played it. Now I would like to see the second part. (Laughter.) : I see.

You know? So I was sitting, so I reach over and get a look and see what the second part looks like. After I see that, now let me see the third part, you know. And I was sitting there, and I'm looking, and a man comes by, you know, just and the harmonies, and because while I'm playing (laughs) that I know, I'm sitting playing. I hear you playing. I know when you make a mistake what I see, that's not what's there. I know what's there. Because I saw it, you know. I can hear it, and I know what's supposed to be there.

And -- but I don't jump on you, because I -- you know. It did me good to know, for some reason, why -- I don't know. If you ask me now why did you have to know? I couldn't answer you. You know? But I like to know, and he was right, or he was wrong.
: It's part of the whole picture.
Yeah, yeah. I guess. I don't know.
So that was the thing, sitting there with Fletcher -- I mean with Charlie, and --
